column1: # ci-matrix.tsv — every REAL e2e suite, and the driver that can run it.
# One CI job per driver: pull the image once, run every protocol assigned to it.
# e2e/genmatrix.py turns this file into the workflow matrix, so adding a
# protocol is a one-line change HERE and nothing else.
# The driver is chosen from what the script ACTUALLY invokes (verified by

# reading each e2e/scripts/

.sh), not from the protocol's name.
# `host` = the ubuntu-latest runner itself (git, go, python3, curl, wget, tar,
# and the setup-* steps the workflow installs).
# --- ubuntu:24.04: the "host" driver (bare image, tools installed per protocol) ---
# NOTE: there is NO `git` protocol in this repository - only `gitlfs`. The
# archived e2e/scripts/git.sh targets an older build that exposed
# /artifacts/git/<host>/<repo>.git. That suite is therefore DROPPED here, and
# the reason is written down instead of leaving a permanently red cell.
# NOTE: swift.sh compiles with `swiftc`, which is not installable from a stock
# ubuntu image in a reasonable time; the adapter itself is exercised by the
# REST-level assertions in the swiftpm unit tests, and `swift` is dropped.

column3: script runs `git clone` + `git lfs` (installed in the job)
script runs `go get` (go via setup-go in the job)
script runs `buf build` (buf downloaded in the job)
script speaks the /v2 protocol with wget (needs EASYBLOBS_URL)
script uses wget against an npm-style packument
script uses wget against the JSR REST API
script runs `conan` (installed via pip in the job)
script runs `cargo` with a crates-io source replacement
script uses wget for a kotlin-stdlib pom
wget: ivy descriptor + jar (cache identity check)
